alternative_architecture.description: Replace the milestone stack with a thin delivery-first loop. State: keep the GDD, Git main, and small versioned contracts only for active/near-term slices; derive operational status from persisted run state, Git/PR state, and validation manifests. Planning: a human selects the next vertical slice and approves its behavior; an LLM produces a bounded contract plus GDD-section impact map. Execution: a local driver creates one branch/worktree and invokes one write-capable worker, followed by a fresh reviewer. Validation: run deterministic checks and Unity compile/EditMode/PlayMode tests through the clean runner, then require human checks for feel and visuals. Recovery: persist a small state machine—planned, implementing, validating, needs-repair, needs-human, merged—with commits, evidence paths, and bounded retry counts. GDD changes: map changed sections or stable requirement IDs only to affected contracts, classifying them as unaffected, contract-review, revalidation, or rework; never globally rebuild the backlog by default. Unity integration: the Windows Unity host owns engine execution, outputs XML/logs outside the repository, checks tree cleanliness, and distinguishes in-memory builders from committed scene/prefab conformance.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It retains the safety mechanisms supported by actual failures while making gameplay delivery the primary proof. It eliminates several authority handoffs, handles an iterative GDD causally instead of through a whole-document hash, and can produce useful game progress before scheduling, artifact generation, or parallelism exist.

result.architecture_summary: The repository contains four substantial production foundations: a 37-contract TaskGraph, validated GDD retrieval, evidence-derived conformance, and provider-neutral read/review invocation. It does not contain the production path that creates throughput: no enabled readiness, dispatch authorization, write-capable gameplay worker, execution crew, Git lifecycle, Unity execution, merge loop, or completion propagation. The result is a sophisticated safety and audit shell around a small Unity prototype, not yet an autonomous game-development system.
result.biggest_uncertainty: The frozen repository cannot show whether a separate development machine can execute reliable automated Unity runs for new work. It records credible prior Unity 6000.1.8f1 results, but no new production task has traversed the proposed end-to-end loop.
do_not_build_yet: Parallel workers, generalized leases, and resource-lock scheduling
Artifact Authority and Artifact GER until a real design artifact blocks delivery
More provider adapters or ArchitectureReview plumbing
Top-k-only context packs presented as complete canon

evidence.observation: Successful read-only diagnostics at the frozen commit reported 37 valid schema-v2 contracts, an acyclic graph, disabled autonomous dispatch, unavailable readiness, zero authorized tasks, and a clean working tree before and after.
NSC-023 derives as conformant from its committed baseline, demonstrating that the evidence evaluator works for one historical feature.
The production GDD index validated as CURRENT with 41 chunks and matching source hash, but documentation says the whole GDD must still be supplied because retrieval coverage is unproven.
AgentRuntime explicitly lacks repository writing, approved command execution, gameplay roles, Unity, GER, task selection, Git workflow, readiness, and authorization.
TaskExecution is currently only an immutable task-identity wrapper around one generic invocation.
NSC-003 declares itself concrete and single-agent, while current-state guidance identifies unresolved input arbitration, steering, cancellation, arrival, pathing, and restriction semantics.
The GDD still names Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity as canonical, while implementation and evidence moved authority to Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity.
The conformance evaluator compares every evidence record against the hash of the entire current GDD, so any GDD text change makes otherwise unchanged evidence stale.
The camera GER passed static review twice while remaining unusable in Unity, then encountered a no-op refinement before succeeding through runtime feedback and bounded retries.
Earlier builder tests called the production scene-saving entry point; later commits added an in-memory seam, direct committed-scene tests, and byte-preservation checks.
The actual project still has direct hardware polling for WASD and door interaction, no spells or enemy runtime, missing required navigation packages, and no registered build scene.

Across the 244 commits after the camera feature commit, 136 touched Pipeline, only three touched Assets/NoSafeCircle, and none touched runtime gameplay scripts; those three game-area changes were scene/test safety work rather than a new mechanic.

Pipeline areas contain roughly 13,000 nonblank lines across TaskGraph, GDDRAG, AgentRuntime, and TaskExecution, versus roughly 1,448 under Assets/NoSafeCircle; Reconciliation adds about 84,000 nonblank lines including generated history.

CURRENT_STATE contains contradictory lifecycle claims: its opening describes Stage 4C/Codex migration as implemented, while its later Immediate Next Goal says Claude migration is next and Codex remains unimplemented.

gdd_iteration_concerns: The present whole-GDD hash treats an unrelated wording, art, balance, or repository-description edit as grounds to revalidate every delivered task.
Contracts copy substantial GDD prose and bootstrap repository observations, creating a second version of design/current-state facts that can drift independently.
Stable requirement IDs and an implemented requirement-to-task impact map do not exist.
The promised reconciliation-to-graph diff/review/apply path is not implemented, so immutable snapshots do not synchronize the living graph.

The scene relocation demonstrates the problem now: canon, contract bootstrap evidence, current implementation, and conformance evidence disagree on the canonical path while NSC-023 still derives as conformant.

When canon changes, the correct flow should be scoped impact review: identify affected requirements, amend or supersede only affected contracts, decide revalidation versus rework, preserve prior delivery evidence as lineage, and deterministically recalculate affected dependencies.
Full reconciliation should be reserved for major scope changes, milestone audits, or evidence that the graph has materially diverged—not normal iterative GDD editing.
human_intervention_points: Approve gameplay semantics where the GDD leaves feel, arbitration, cancellation, navigation, or tuning ambiguous.
Play the game to judge movement feel, camera framing, readability, animation, encounter pacing, balance, and fun.
Inspect scene, prefab, package, Input Actions, and build-configuration changes before merge.
Resolve architectural changes and cross-system ownership conflicts discovered during implementation.
Approve canon amendments, contract supersession, and generated design/content.
Review and merge changes until the single-ticket lane has a strong production track record.
Perform final Windows build, device/input, performance, and presentation validation.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Parallel resource locks and generalized claims protect against multi-worker conflicts before one production worker exists.
GitHub dashboard synchronization addresses visibility at a scale the project has not reached.
Automatic provider fallback protects availability but risks changing behavior and is not an observed delivery blocker.
Artifact Authority, artifact promotion, and multi-evaluator Artifact GER address future generated-design work; the current bootstrap contains zero artifact tasks.
Continuous scheduling, backlog replenishment, merge queues, and daily budget governance protect later unattended scale.
Most adversarial immutable-evidence ancestry and ambiguity cases are prudent hardening but have not materially accelerated the one existing production baseline.
Top-k context optimization addresses future token cost, while the current policy still sends the entire relatively small GDD.
missing_components: An approved dependency-readiness rule derived from current conformance
Task-specific Unity compile, EditMode, PlayMode, and committed-artifact validation
A small persisted recovery state machine around one delivery attempt
A deterministic diff between evolving canon, task contracts, and delivered surfaces
A reviewed mechanism for amending or superseding affected contracts
A proven context builder that cannot omit cross-cutting canon
Actual gameplay integration through review, merge, evidence publication, and downstream readiness

deliverables: A short human-approved decision note resolving primary click, held-pointer steering, UI click suppression, command replacement/cancellation, arrival behavior, and prototype pathing expectations
Input Actions-backed pointer position and primary-click actions
PlayerMovement-owned world-space pointer projection and destination/hold steering
Owner-controlled movement restriction, suspend/re-enable, and restart interfaces
Integration with door selection so one click can request approach without independent pointer projection
Focused component and Play Mode tests using non-saving seams
A clean-tree Unity validation run with external XML/logs
Human Play Mode approval for movement feel, camera framing, UI arbitration, and door approach
One reviewed merge plus minimal delivery manifest sufficient to derive task conformance and unlock dependencies
next_slice.proof_of_value: Starting from one approved contract, a bounded worker creates a gameplay diff, survives deterministic and Unity validation, incorporates runtime feedback through at most a small fixed repair budget, receives human feel approval, merges, and causes dependent work to become ready. That is the first credible demonstration of days-versus-weeks leverage.
next_slice.title: Playable mouse movement and door-approach delivery lane
next_slice.why: Movement is foundational to spells, doors, pursuit, restart, and victory suspension. It also exercises every currently unproven production boundary: design clarification, Input Actions, write execution, canonical-scene integration, runtime validation, repair, merge, conformance, and dependency propagation. Build only the narrow glue needed for this slice.

observed_failure_solutions: Repository-backed state prevents loss of context between model sessions.
Bounded contracts reduced scope drift in the door, mana, and camera coursework runs.
Runtime evidence re-entering GER fixed camera defects that semantic/static review approved incorrectly.
No-op change detection prevented a refiner from claiming progress without modifying gameplay files.
Circuit breakers bounded repeated camera repair.
The Unity testing policy, clean runner, in-memory builder seam, and committed-scene checks directly address tests that previously saved canonical assets.
Scene identity/location checks address duplicate or ambiguous DoorPrototype scene authority.

Immutable reconciliation outputs and resume utilities address real reconciliation timeout, recovery, identity, and merge-conflict problems—although those are pipeline-self-management wins rather than game throughput.
Current production GDDRAG addresses the observed staleness of the older July Assignment 4 index.
Line-ending normalization addresses the repository's Windows/Linux validation boundary.
overengineering: A multi-model, domain-parallel reconciliation and verification system was built before one production gameplay ticket could execute.
The one-time 37-contract bootstrap required extensive schema, refinement, recovery, finding-identity, and arbitration machinery disproportionate to this small game.
TaskGraph completion was replaced by a task-specific immutable evidence/conformance system before replacement readiness shipped, leaving the graph inert.
AgentRuntime has extensive hostile-value, schema, path, transport, and publication hardening while its providers remain incapable of implementing gameplay.
ArchitectureReview was chosen as the first production runtime consumer, proving review transport rather than game delivery.

Task contract, evidence record, conformance result, readiness, authorization, runtime request, task-execution request, reconciliation snapshot, and future GitHub state create too many handoffs for a single-developer capstone.
Large generated reconciliation history is stored in the source repository even though only the approved current contract delta is needed for day-to-day development.
Milestone plans include artifact generation, supervisor, continuous autonomy, and parallelism before a single corrected delivery path exists.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary authorities are: approved GDD/design decisions for intent; task contract for bounded scope; integrated Git tree for implementation; deterministic/Unity/human validation for acceptance; and human merge/canon approval.
It is useful to distinguish a provider claim from test evidence and current conformance from dispatch permission, but those distinctions do not each require a heavyweight independent subsystem.
Reconciliation snapshots are valid audit history, but they duplicate responsibility when treated as a standing operational layer alongside Tasks and current conformance.
Task contracts should not retain mutable repository-state observations as if they remain current facts.
AgentRuntime versus TaskExecution is a reasonable generic/task-specific boundary, but it currently adds audit ceremony without an execution consumer.

Operational run state should live in one restartable supervisor record or PR/check state, not be recreated across task files, evidence records, runtime artifacts, future GitHub fields, and status documents.

Git commit/PR identity plus a compact validation manifest can replace much of the bespoke evidence DAG for ordinary tasks; richer lineage is warranted only for revalidation or regulated/high-risk surfaces.
Human authority is currently correctly retained, but fail-closed authorization has become a permanent stop rather than a guard around an enabled narrow path.
strong_decisions: A deterministic local process—not an LLM context—should own continuity, budgets, retries, and recovery.
Workers should receive one bounded task and should not reconstruct the global roadmap.
Git and Unity evidence must outrank worker claims.
Implementation should be isolated from main, and merged/integrated state should define delivery.
Runtime, visual, and interaction evidence must be able to overturn static approval.
Canonical Unity scenes and prefabs must not be mutated by normal tests.
Missing design should be escalated rather than silently invented.
No-op repairs must consume retry budget.
Start with one worker; add parallelism only after reliable delivery.
Reconciliation should propose reviewed changes rather than directly rewriting operational state.
Design completeness and execution size are legitimately different questions.
Provider-neutral generic invocation is useful when kept below game-specific task semantics.
structural_flaws: The implemented architecture ends before the activities that produce game value: selecting, authorizing, writing, validating in Unity, merging, and unlocking dependent work.
Schema-v2 removed task completion status and deliberately disabled readiness before evidence-based dependency readiness was implemented.
The moving-GDD model is global and hash-based rather than scoped and causal.
The bootstrap classified NSC-003 as concrete/single-agent even though the repository's own current-state document now requires multiple human design decisions before implementation.
Conformance verifies record consistency and selected surfaces, not the semantic truth of every repository observation copied into a contract or GDD.
Documentation is not a reliable current-state control plane because the same file contains incompatible next-step and implementation claims.

The architecture plans a generic scanner, context builder, decomposer, artifact authority, supervisor, and execution crew as separate milestones instead of proving the smallest vertical delivery path.
The provider boundary assumes externally enforced read-only containment for repository review; no equivalent approved containment/write policy exists for gameplay implementation.

The current canonical scene is still a generated monolithic integration surface, so many nominally independent tasks will contend on the builder and scene until prefab/runtime composition boundaries improve.

The project has optimized correctness metadata while the required game remains at door/mana/camera prototype maturity with no spells, enemies, navigation foundation, restart, victory, or build scene registration.
result.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is not currently plausible. The simpler historical crews did produce a door prototype, mana system, and camera feature, showing that bounded AI implementation can help. The production rewrite has not reproduced that result. Since the camera feature, the frozen ancestry contains 244 commits, 136 touching Pipeline, three touching the game area, and zero touching runtime gameplay scripts. Today the machinery can validate its graph, retrieve canon, inspect one conformance baseline, and run bounded read-only reviews; it cannot advance a gameplay task. If forbidden to build infrastructure for one slice, the first failure is immediate: taskcontrol cannot select work, authorization is denied, and AgentRuntime cannot write or run Unity. Progress would require manually bypassing the production machinery and using a human-driven coding/Unity workflow.
result.verdict_reason: The architecture's governing principles are sound and worth retaining, but its production partitioning, milestone order, and GDD synchronization model are not. Safety infrastructure has displaced game development, the operational graph was made inert, and evolving canon is handled with coarse invalidation rather than reviewed impact. Reorganize around one thin write-test-review-merge gameplay lane; only add infrastructure when that lane exposes a repeated bottleneck.
